Updates every second from your computer’s clock, including offline. Keep the clock synchronized. Selected locations use mapped time zones and your browser’s daylight-saving rules; open-ocean points use nautical time. Daylight uses an average sunrise/sunset threshold of −0.833°; twilight boundaries are −6°, −12°, and −18°. Atmospheric conditions and terrain can change the visible horizon. 07

Read the signals

A quick guide to the numbers inside the banners.

SFI / SNSolar activity

SFI is solar radio flux; SN is sunspot number. Higher activity often helps the higher HF bands, but neither number guarantees a usable path.

K / AGeomagnetic conditions

These indices describe geomagnetic disturbance over different periods. Lower values generally favor steadier HF propagation; larger disturbances can disrupt paths.

MUFA station measurement

Maximum usable frequency depends on the path. A banner’s ionosonde location is a reference, not a personalized forecast for Panama City. NoRpt indicates an unavailable report.

D / NDay and night

HF predictions separate daylight from darkness. The transition between the two is the gray line. Use the daylight maps to explore paths near that boundary.

EMEMoonbounce conditions

EME degradation estimates additional loss for Earth–Moon–Earth work. Lower loss is preferable. The Moon-facing globe shows the Earth as viewed from the Moon.

UTCCheck the printed time

Each banner carries its own data timestamp. Loading an image now does not mean every measurement is current. The clocks above show the time now; the image timestamps describe the source data.

Your station

Personalize this page. No account or server needed.

The default is Panama City’s approximate center. Saved coordinates set the solar times, bearings, grid, and NWS weather requests.

The MUF selector changes the single-station value on compatible panels; it does not replace the locations on the world MUF map. Source images retain their native size when space allows. Your browser may shrink them to fit a smaller screen.

Export includes station settings, banner order, custom links, scratchpad, net reminders, and the local contact log. Backups from the earlier version can also be imported. Keep the HTML file at the same location to help your browser retain its settings. Export before moving it or changing browsers.

A home for your station

Using your local homepage

  1. Save Ham-Radio-Home.html somewhere permanent on your computer and open it in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari.
  2. Bookmark the page, or copy its file:///… address into your browser’s homepage or startup-page settings. Some browsers need an extension to customize the new-tab page.
  3. Select Choose banners to pick any of the 23 HamQSL formats. Move cards with their up/down arrows or remove a card with its × button.
  4. Open My station to set your callsign, time zone, and appearance. Export setup if you want to transfer your settings and notes.

Live images, local page

The HTML, clocks, notes, and calculator work without a web server. Banners load directly from HamQSL and need an internet connection. Online links also need internet. There is no bundled snapshot of current conditions.

Refresh & data age

Automatic refresh runs hourly while the page is open. Sleeping computers and background tabs may delay timers; the page checks again when you return. Reload panels retries the selected images. Always check the UTC time printed inside each banner; individual measurements can be unavailable or older than the image.

Live world daylight

The World daylight map, world clocks, and location statuses recalculate every second from the current UTC time. All coastline data and calculations are embedded, so the map also works offline. Select a city or click a point to inspect it; keyboard arrows move the selected point, and Home returns to your station.

The live map handles the date line, seasonal tilt, polar day and night, and three twilight bands. Keep the device clock synchronized. Daylight uses the standard −0.833° sunrise/sunset approximation, accounting for the solar disk and average refraction; terrain and actual atmospheric conditions can shift the visible horizon.

New station tools

The live desk adds NOAA geomagnetic, radio-blackout, and radiation scales, NWS forecasts and alerts, and local solar times. Expand NOAA propagation plots for Kp, X-rays, solar-wind speed, and magnetic Bz. Live data is requested every 15 minutes while open, and each source keeps its own timestamp.

Use the planner for grid-to-grid headings, editable daily or weekly nets, and the contact log. Contact exports are available in ADIF and CSV. The beacon clock shows scheduled slots based on your device clock, without checking whether a beacon is transmitting. Keep your computer’s time synchronized.

Antenna lengths are starting estimates. The RF calculator separates line loss from mismatch. The interval timer runs in this page, and the Morse practice tool plays sound through your speakers.

Credits

Solar panels are provided by Paul L. Herrman, N0NBH / HamQSL. Original artwork, credit lines, and links are preserved. Underlying contributors are identified on HamQSL and in the panels. See the HamQSL FAQ for source details and available options.

Additional sources: NOAA SWPC, National Weather Service, NOAA solar calculations, NCDXF/IARU beacon project, and the linked local club sources. Contact exports follow ADIF 3.1.4.

Privacy & saving

Station details, links, notes, net reminders, and contacts are stored in this browser when available. The live desk requests NOAA data and sends the saved coordinates to NWS to obtain forecasts and alerts. Contacts and notes are not uploaded to these services. Loading a remote banner contacts its host; opening a resource visits that site. Private browsing, clearing site data, moving the file, or browser restrictions may remove or isolate saved settings. Use Export setup for a portable backup.
